generator.params.note: From giant horsetail's (equisetum-telmateia) params, changed for scouring rush: no whorled branches, so each node's whorl is its sheath's teeth, the leaves themselves (Equisetaceae: leaves a whorl of teeth joined into a sheath), as many as leaves_per_whorl gives by the rule, 5 mm long (leaf_length, the model's leaf length), pressed to the stem (leaf_angle 10) and the same size from foot to tip (leaf_top, leaf_base 1); straight, stiff, nearly upright stems (stem_lean 4, wiggle 0.5) about 8 mm thick (stem_radius 0.004, by eye), sheathed from near the ground (bare 0.05), about 20 nodes; more stems in a wider clump for its dense colonies (stems 20, clump_radius 0.3); stem_height from height_typical_m by the rule instead of by hand; leaf_years 2 so a stem stands through its first winter (FNA: aerial stems persisting more than a year). leaf_area left to the shading test, its blade card now broader (aspect 0.25). No cones: the program draws none on a stem without a raceme. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.9 m tall at 4 years in the open, within the Flora of North America's 18 to 220 cm. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours by eye from the source words: dark green stems (the bark; the species' usual description, no source read gives a stem colour beyond evergreen); the whorls of teeth, standing for the sheaths, ash grey (Fern Grower's Manual: a wide ash-gray band between a lower black band and an upper black rim; FNA: sheaths dark-girdled, brown to gray above girdle), shaded near black.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_typical_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine, the subspecies in North America (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Aerial stems persisting more than a year, unbranched, 18--220 cm"; erect, so as tall as long.

traits.height_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Aerial stems ... 18--220 cm"; the greatest, 2.2 m (the model's record L2902170 gives 2 m).

traits.leaf_habit.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001), Equisetum hyemale: evergreen (ref fern-2026-10-15#1069). Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Aerial stems persisting more than a year".

traits.branching.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Aerial stems ... unbranched"; "old stems sometimes developing branches with cones in spring". Fern Grower's Manual (ref fern-2026-10-15#1069): usually unbranched.

traits.leaves_per_whorl.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "teeth 14--50, articulate and promptly shed or persistent"; each tooth is a leaf's free tip, the leaves joined below into the sheath (Equisetaceae). The trait counts to 40, so the range stops there.

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2902170), as no source read gives it: the free teeth 2 to 5 mm.

traits.leaf_division.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2902170), as no source read gives it.

traits.rosette.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2902170), as no source read gives it.

traits.perennation.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L2902170), as no source read gives it; the Fern Grower's Manual (ref fern-2026-10-15#1069) gives the rhizome long-creeping.

traits.cone_apex.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Cone apex pointed"; Fern Grower's Manual (ref fern-2026-10-15#1069): a minute point.

traits.habit_notes.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001), Equisetum hyemale: medium to large scouring rush forming large colonies (ref fern-2026-10-15#1069).

traits.light.note: Hoshizaki and Moran, Fern Grower's Manual (2001), Equisetum hyemale: sun, usually (ref fern-2026-10-15#1069).

traits.moisture.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Moist roadsides, riverbanks, lakeshores, woodlands".

traits.habitat_notes.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "Moist roadsides, riverbanks, lakeshores, woodlands; 0--3000 m"; Fern Grower's Manual (ref fern-2026-10-15#1069): shaded riverbanks, railroad ballast.

traits.elevation_min_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "0--3000 m".

traits.elevation_max_m.note: Flora of North America vol. 2 (1993), Equisetum hyemale subsp. affine (read on eFloras, 2026-10-18): "0--3000 m".

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy added with the core-species expansion, batch A1 (2026-10-18): sizes and forms from the Flora of North America (subsp. affine) and the Fern Grower's Manual, gaps from the model's record.

traits.habit_notes: Medium to large scouring rush forming large colonies of stiff, evergreen, usually unbranched stems.
traits.habitat_notes: Moist roadsides, riverbanks, lakeshores and woodlands; shaded riverbanks and railroad ballast.
